actions.effect: The Pack gains +1 Feed and the actor's holder gains +1 Feed (the hunt feeds the Pack and the camp; the hunters are the Pack, and the Legion provisions them). The hunting Engine's Hunger -2 (minimum 0). The Engine is the one the actor rides or commands in the fork; beyond Brigus-Sledge the Pack's Engines are a shared pool for action purposes (see fork_assumptions).

The split feeds both pools: the Pack gets enough for Dream Share, the Legion gets its hunt income back. Forage stays the floor. Instinct routing is unchanged (the plan's rule, pilot's faction).

drift_checks.rule: No new Seed Core origins. Where the first Seed Cores came from is a sealed open mystery; the engine never answers it, and no action, clock, or legacy rule may reference an origin.

No resolving open mysteries: Seed Core origins; the Deepmaw migration destination; what happens to a pilot whose Engine dies. None of these appears in the action catalog, the clocks, or the legacy rules.
No retroactive changes to Turns 1-136. The fork starts at Turn 131 vFINAL; nothing in the fork rewrites campaign history, and no event may reference a turn after 131 as a past fact.
No touching the Krov decision or the Turn 136 scene. No sequel clock, sequel actor, or sequel location may appear in the seed or the DB. The manifest lists every excluded sequel item.
No resurrecting the Rift-King or the Den Boss. Both are dead; neither appears as an actor, and no action may bring either back.

Bond changes only by the established rules: Pack Merge burns Bond -2 per Engine; Dream Share restores Bond +1 to one Engine per Dream Share at a cost of 2 Feed from the Pack, never above 5 (v1.4, Bryan's call, option C); no other action changes Bond; Bond 0 means the Engine will not move for that pilot.

No new named NPCs, Engines, or locations. Role labels in the seed (Caravan Master, Dust-Baron Captain, Breaker Poacher Chief, Legion Captain) are fork labels, never presented as canon names. The engine never names a new character.

The High Baron's fate is not resolved by the engine. His fork movements (bargain chain) are fork events only. The engine must not declare a blood-oath taken, an execution, or a release as a canon fact.
Clocks never decrease. Clocks advance only via events, and complete only at max. No action in the catalog lowers a clock.
The Concord camp is never named Chalk Canyons in the fork. Chalk Canyons is the Nest-Keeper's canyon (Turns 127-129); the Concord camp is the chained-hauler fortress two days south.
Goliath's left mortar pod stays destroyed (Turn 112). No repair or legacy rule restores it.
Brigus's Turn 114 to 115 recovery jump stays unexplained. The engine must not invent a heal event for it.
Locations are never deleted. Controller and status change only via events, with old and new values recorded, so a later dynamic map can render destroyed or flipped regions instead of losing them.
Only the 16 registry entries (IW-42 to IW-85) exist as mechanics. Only IW-42 is on the dormant watchlist; IW-46 and IW-84 stay resolved from the final arc. No new mechanic may appear.
The fork label appears on every output (event log, world view, run notes) so the test world is never confused with the live timeline.

Core identity holds: Ironwild is Zoids mixed with Gaogaigar at its core (Bryan, 2026-11-20). Beast-machines, Bonds, and brave-hearted combining heroics. The engine must not drift the world into generic mecha: no piloted humanoid robots, no generic 'mech' language in the render, no combining sequence that forgets the Bond cost. The master bible already records this DNA ('Influences (DNA only, no canon imports): Zoids, Gaogaigar'); Bryan's 23:17 statement confirms it in his own words.

Quiet-world fix actions (forage, scavenge, claim) are fork-supplied mechanics only. They add no canon, do not change the Turn 131 freeze, do not touch the Krov decision, and do not restore Bond. Claim can never take a controlled location. Dream Share is a scored action (v1.5), not a rest hook; it fires while an unmapped location exists or an Engine's Bond is below 5.

Bond recovery happens only through Dream Share, only +1 Bond to one Engine per Dream Share (the lowest Bond, ties to Sledge), only at a cost of 2 Feed from the Pack, and never above 5. No other action restores Bond. Seedborns stay extremely rare: Brigus is the only Seedborn in the fork; no other Seedborn is added. Their powers are heavy: restoring Bond is strong and costly, never free.

v1.6 (Bryan's call, supersedes v1.5 hunt routing): Hunt Feed splits +1 to the Pack and +1 to the actor's holder. Dream Share remains a scored action, not a rest hook. Bond branch rules unchanged from v1.4 (+1 to lowest Bond, ties to Sledge, 2 Feed from the Pack, never above 5). Freeze unchanged (Turn 131 vFINAL).

v1.6 economy guards: forage is the Legion's Feed floor (no other action's Feed routing changes); Instinct routes to the pilot's faction per the plan's rule (the seed does not change it); scavenge is unchanged (the Legion variant fires; the Dust Baron and Breakers variants do not fire for good reasons - see fork_assumptions). No other action's trigger or effect changes in v1.6.

legacy_rules.name: Aging
legacy_rules.rule: Every NPC ages +1 year at the era boundary. No NPC is flagged old in this seed (no ages are established in canon), so no retirement or death fires from aging in Phase 1. If Lore flags an NPC old in a later seed, the aging rule retires or kills them by that flag, and the engine logs it.

legacy_rules.name: Molt on earned triggers
legacy_rules.rule: Any Engine with an earned, unspent Molt trigger Molts at the boundary: form changes per the trigger, Hunger resets to 0, status becomes molted. A Molt trigger is earned only by consuming a feral core (Turn 129: Skytalon consumed the feral core and triggered Adult Molt). No Molt trigger is earned at tick 0.

legacy_rules.name: Succession
legacy_rules.rule: If an NPC died during the era, their Bonds and holdings pass to their named successor (see actors.successor). Only Vance names a successor (Tull). If the dead NPC names no successor, the engine STOPS and asks Lore instead of improvising. Brigus names no successor: no heir is named in canon.

legacy_rules.name: Dormant Cores confirmed
legacy_rules.rule: Any dormant Seed Core found during the era is confirmed in its holder's Cores pool at the boundary. Cores are 0 everywhere at tick 0; they enter the pool only when found.

legacy_rules.name: Era applied once
legacy_rules.rule: The era row is marked applied exactly once at the boundary. A second application in the same era is a test failure.

fork_assumptions: Starting resource quantities are fork-supplied. Canon gives no numbers for Salvage, Feed, Cores, or Territory at vFINAL.
Starting Hunger values (Sledge 3, Skytalon 2, Razor-Back 3, Goliath 1, Strider 1) are fork-supplied. Canon gives Hunger types, not numbers.
Hunger types for Skytalon (hunt), Razor-Back (territory), Goliath (wreckage), and Strider (speed) are fork assignments. Only Sledge's type (protective) is attested in canon.
The Legion Cohesion and Great Basin Recovery clocks are fork-supplied. The absorbed mercenaries and the siege-scarred city are canon; the clocks themselves are the fork's test variables.
The High Baron's bargain chain (guarded to watched to free, then leaves for Rust Dunes) is a fork-supplied rule. Canon gives only his state.
Role labels for unnamed actors (Caravan Master, Dust-Baron Captain, Breaker Poacher Chief, Legion Captain) are fork labels, not canon names.
Pilot assignments beyond Brigus-Sledge are null in canon. The Pack's Engines are a shared pool for action purposes in the fork; the engine must not assign a pilot without Lore approval.
Vance names Tull as successor. That is a fork assignment; no other actor names a successor.

Shape mappings: Razor-Back and Strider are mapped to Stalker, Goliath to Bulwark. The plan's shape enum (Stalker/Bulwark/Skytalon/Deepmaw) has no tracked-chassis or Dreadnought value; flagged as a schema gap in the manifest.
Great Basin kind is 'city', a requested schema extension. The plan's kind enum (caravan/den/nest/wreck) has no city value.
The Feed burn rate for the city and the Pack is NOT set in this seed. Canon gives no burn rate. The Engine Team sets it, or asks Lore; the engine must not invent a canon burn rate.
The 'fortified' status value for Great Basin is introduced by the Recovery clock's completion effect. It is a fork status value, not a canon term.

The forage action (Legion Captain, Legion Feed below 4, +2 Feed) is a fork-supplied mechanic (v1.3 quiet-world fix). The campaign never defines how the Legion feeds itself; the rate is a test parameter, not canon.

The scavenge action (holder Salvage below 4, mapped wreck exists, +1 Salvage) is a fork-supplied mechanic (v1.3 quiet-world fix). Stripping the war's wreckage for parts is canon-consistent; the rate is a test parameter, not canon.

The claim action (uncontrolled mapped location, holder Salvage 1 or more, controller becomes the actor's faction, Salvage -1) is a fork-supplied mechanic (v1.3 quiet-world fix) to prove controller flips. It cannot take a controlled location. Bond recovery exists only through Dream Share (v1.4, Bryan's call, option C): +1 Bond to one Engine per Dream Share, Pack Feed -2, never above 5.

Seedborns are extremely rare in the world (Bryan, 2026-11-20): Brigus is the only Seedborn in Fork A; no other Seedborn is added to the fork. Their powers are heavy: Dream Share restores Bond at a heavy Feed cost.

Hunt Feed goes to the Pack (v1.5, combined fix option 1): the hunters are the Pack, so the hunt feeds the Pack. v1.0-v1.4 routed hunt Feed to the actor's holder (the Legion for Brigus, Vance, Tull, Kaelen; the Nest-Keepers for the Nest-Keeper), which starved the Pack's Feed pool - no action ever gave the Pack Feed - and left Dream Share's Bond branch unable to fire. The Legion's Feed now comes from forage; the rerun should watch the Legion's Feed.

Dream Share is a scored action (v1.5, combined fix option 3), not a rest hook: Brigus chooses it as his action for the tick, scored by its material effect. It no longer requires Brigus to rest. The Bond branch rules are unchanged from v1.4.

Hunt Feed splits +1 Pack / +1 actor's holder (v1.6, Bryan's call): v1.5 routed all hunt Feed to the Pack, which fixed the Pack but starved the Legion (Legion Feed ended at 0, trade collapsed to 28, forage alone at 108 fires could not sustain it) and flooded the Pack to 698 Feed. The split feeds both pools: the Pack gets enough for Dream Share, the Legion gets its hunt income back. Forage stays the floor. Instinct routing is unchanged (the plan's rule, pilot's faction). Scavenge is unchanged (the Legion variant fires 254 times in the v1.5 run; the Dust Baron and Breakers variants do not fire for good reasons - his Salvage is not low, they recover Salvage by raiding).

map_state.note: FUTURE REQUIREMENT (Phase 4 / Companion, NOT Phase 1 scope): the world view map must eventually become DYNAMIC. If a continent gets wiped out, a territory flips, a den falls, or a region is destroyed, the change must be visible on the map. This section is the source the dynamic map will read. Location control and status changes are recorded as events with old and new values, and locations are never deleted (see drift rule DC-13), so a destroyed region renders as destroyed, not vanished. Phase 1 keeps the static HTML world view; no dynamic map is built here.

resource_definitions.Cores: Dormant Seed Cores. Zero everywhere at tick 0. The Den Boss's dormant Core (locked in his shack at Turn 62) has no established fate; the fork does NOT assume the Pack holds it. Dormant Cores enter the pool only when found during play, per the legacy rules.
resource_definitions.Feed: Food and fuel for Engines and people. Engines consume Feed when fed; the city consumes Feed every tick (see action effects; the Engine Team sets the burn rate, Lore does not invent a canon burn rate).
resource_definitions.Salvage: Scrap iron, armor, and war-tech recovered from wrecks and the battlefield. Spent on repairs and fortification.
resource_definitions.Territory: Count of locations a holder controls. Derived from the locations table; the seed values above match the controllers listed (Legion 2, Concord 1, Nest-Keepers 1, all others 0). Unmapped locations are uncontrolled and count for no one.
